title: Dog Parks in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **The lead is the default everywhere.** Since 1 January 2019 Berlin has a citywide leash rule; the only places it comes off are the marked forest areas and the fenced runs, unless you hold a Bestandshund or Sachkunde exemption.

**Twelve forest areas, about 1,220 hectares.** Grunewald, Wannsee-Düppel, Düppel, Kladow, Pichelswerder, Hakenfelde, Jungfernheide, Frohnau and Blankenfelde are run by Berliner Forsten. Outside their signs the lead goes back on, even inside the same forest.

**Fenced runs are small and uneven.** Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg alone publishes nine, between 1,160 and 2,900 m². Fence heights differ: Stralauer Platz has 1.40 m, Wriezener Park and Weidenweg 0.80 m. Check the fence before you unclip a jumper.

**Some greens ban dogs outright.** Playgrounds, Badeanstalten, public bathing spots and marked sunbathing lawns are closed to dogs by law, and Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg adds Weberwiese, Traveplatz, Boxhagener Platz and the Märchenbrunnen.

**The paperwork is one registration.** Hunderegister online costs €17.50 and doubles as the tax registration since 1 January 2024. Hundesteuer is €120 a year for the first dog and €180 for each further dog. Fines run up to €10,000.
**Use the map below from your own station.** Type it in, say whether you need a fence or open forest, and the tool ranks every area by distance.
